comments.content: This change removes the nonce reset after validation. Since `_authNonce` is now a constant generated once at service construction, the same nonce is reused for every auth request for the lifetime of the extension. This weakens the CSRF/state protection: a previously observed `state` value remains valid indefinitely and can be replayed. Consider rotating the nonce per auth request (and resetting it after successful validation) rather than making it a fixed readonly value.

The state mismatch is now only a warning that the user can dismiss by choosing "Store". Combined with the nonce no longer being reset/rotated, this effectively removes the state validation guarantee. An attacker who can trigger the auth callback URI with an arbitrary token and a mismatched state can get the user to store an attacker-controlled token. At minimum, keep the hard failure for mismatched state, or clearly scope the bypass to the intended external-signin flow (e.g. only when no auth request is in progress).
